title: 11D Projection / Reconstruction / Information Unification — Developed Theory
status: older project archaeology + developed inverse-problem and compactification research programme
abstract: The 11D branch is strongest when treated as a theory of descriptions rather than a numbered metaphysical ladder. A high-dimensional state X can generate many lower-dimensional descriptions Y_d through projection, coarse-graining, observation or compactification. The scientific problem is then precise: which features survive, which are erased, which can be reconstructed, and what additional assumptions are required to infer hidden structure from an observed lower-dimensional state? This redevelopment turns that idea into an explicit inverse-problem framework. It defines projection channels, fibers and equivalence classes, task-specific sufficiency, Bayes-optimal reconstruction, rate-distortion and Blackwell ordering of descriptions. It then separates this information-theoretic branch from physical 11D-to-4D compactification, where an action, metric ansatz, internal seven-manifold, moduli, fluxes, truncation and four-dimensional spectrum are required. The project's Door becomes a typed interface between descriptions rather than an automatic fifth spatial dimension. The central nontrivial question is no longer 'what is dimension 7 or 8?' but whether a proposed lower description is sufficient for a task, whether two projections are comparable or incomparable, and whether a physical compactification derives rather than merely resembles the observed low-energy theory. The framework is T2 as mathematics and T1 as physical 11D unification.
research_question: Given a concrete high-dimensional state space and family of reductions, what information and invariants are preserved, what reconstruction error is unavoidable, and can a physical 11D compactification derive a viable 4D spectrum rather than merely organize labels?

core_objects.ambient: X in P, where P is either an 11D spacetime/configuration space or a high-dimensional statistical state space
core_objects.fiber: F_y=pi_d^-1(y), the set of high-dimensional states indistinguishable at the lower description
core_objects.task: Z, a target/observable whose preservation defines whether a reduction is useful
core_objects.rule: physical spacetime, statistical state space and information channel interpretations must be typed separately

inverse_problem_formulation.meaning: reconstruction is never just the inverse symbol pi^-1; it is an inference problem over a fiber using a loss and prior/constraint structure

equivalence_and_fibers.quotient_view: the lower description identifies all states inside one equivalence class/fiber
equivalence_and_fibers.hidden_state_dimension: fiber geometry measures the degrees of freedom invisible to the projection
equivalence_and_fibers.door_interpretation: a Door may select, transmit or collapse equivalence classes between representations; this is mathematically meaningful only after its map is declared

information_theory.task_sufficiency: Y is sufficient for Z relative to X when I(Z;X|Y)=0
information_theory.meaning: a lower-dimensional description can lose microscopic information yet preserve everything needed for a particular task

blackwell_ordering.definition: Y2 is a garbling of Y1 when p(y2|x)=sum_y1 K(y2|y1)p(y1|x)
blackwell_ordering.consequence: for every decision problem with the same state X, Y1 cannot have worse optimal Bayes risk than Y2
blackwell_ordering.project_value: this creates a rigorous ordering of some dimensional descriptions without pretending every pair lies on one scalar ladder
blackwell_ordering.incomparability: two projections may preserve different information and be Blackwell-incomparable; one scalar information score cannot universally rank them

projection_scorecard.use: compare candidate reductions as a Pareto problem rather than by dimension number alone

worked_linear_gaussian_model.reconstruction_uncertainty: Tr(Sigma_post) is one quadratic-loss summary of what remains hidden
worked_linear_gaussian_model.meaning: rank, noise and prior covariance determine recoverability; adding dimensions to X does not automatically add recoverable information

differential_geometry_branch.horizontal_choice: a connection chooses a complement H_x to V_x
differential_geometry_branch.holonomy: parallel transport around closed loops may return hidden/internal states transformed
differential_geometry_branch.project_value: this formalizes 'return to the same visible state with changed hidden orientation' without inventing a new visible coordinate

physical_11d_to_4d_branch.starting_point: 11D supergravity comparator with metric g_MN, 3-form C_3 and gravitino psi_M
physical_11d_to_4d_branch.internal_space: compact seven-dimensional X_7 for direct 11D->4D reduction
physical_11d_to_4d_branch.G2_neighbor: G2 holonomy is a structurally appropriate route to 4D minimal supersymmetry in simple fluxless comparators
required_derivation: gauge sectors from geometry/singularities where relevant
physical_11d_to_4d_branch.rule: SO(10,1), OSp(1|32), SU(5), Spin(10) or E8 labels do not substitute for this derivation

kaluza_klein_example.simple_circle: For a field on M4 x S1 with radius R, expand Phi(x,y)=sum_n phi_n(x)e^(iny/R)
kaluza_klein_example.meaning: an extra compact coordinate becomes a tower of four-dimensional modes; this is the concrete sense in which hidden geometric structure can leave a lower-dimensional spectral signature
kaluza_klein_example.lesson: a physical extra dimension earns meaning through its induced spectrum/couplings, not through a symbolic level number

candidate_invariants.topological: Euler characteristic, Betti numbers, index-like quantities may be robust under specific deformations but not arbitrary projections
candidate_invariants.Noether: requires a continuous symmetry of a specified action
candidate_invariants.information: mutual information is generally not invariant under coarse-graining; it usually decreases
candidate_invariants.task_invariant: a target statistic T(X) is preserved exactly if T=T_tilde o pi on the allowed state set
candidate_invariants.research_goal: replace the historical I*(M_d)=I*(M_(d±1)) slogan by one proved invariant for one explicit map

door_as_channel.quantum: rho_out=E_D(rho_in), where E_D must be completely positive and trace preserving for an ordinary quantum channel
door_as_channel.boundary: a quantum channel is not automatically a spatial dimension or wormhole

falsification_and_failure_conditions: A claimed lossless reconstruction fails when two admissible X with different target properties share the same pi(X).
A proposed universal ordering fails when two projections are Blackwell-incomparable or trade reconstruction against task performance.
A claimed invariant fails when an allowed reduction changes it.
A physical compactification fails if its effective 4D spectrum, chirality, couplings or cosmology are inconsistent with observation.
A dimensional theory remains organizational if no map, action, spectrum or observable distinguishes it from a relabeling.
next_decisive_calculations: Build one explicit 11D-or-high-dimensional synthetic state X and at least two competing projections pi_1,pi_2.
Compute posterior reconstruction error and task sufficiency for both reductions.
Test whether one projection is a garbling of the other or whether they are incomparable.
Prove one exact preserved statistic or demonstrate that the historical I* invariant fails.
For the physical branch, derive one compactification spectrum rather than extending the dimensional ladder vocabulary.
